en: The Hymn to Śiva, the Essence of the Vedas (Vedasāraśivastotra)
Śrīḥ.
Now begins the Vedasāraśivastotra (The Hymn to Śiva, the Essence of the Vedas).
To the Lord of creatures, the destroyer of sin, the Supreme Ruler, the most excellent one who wears the skin of the lordly elephant,
with the waters of the Gaṅgā sparkling amidst his mass of matted hair—
I remember Mahādeva alone, the enemy of Smara. || 1 ||
To Maheśa, the Lord of the gods, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods,
the all-pervading Lord of the universe, whose limbs are adorned with divine splendor,
the three-eyed one whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire;
I praise the Lord, the five-faced one, who is eternal bliss. || 2 ||
I bow to Girīśa, Gaṇeśa, whose throat is blue,
who is mounted upon the lord of elephants, whose form transcends all qualities,
who is radiant Bhava, his limbs adorned with ashes.
I worship the five-faced one, whose consort is Bhavānī. || 3 ||
O beloved of Śivā, O Śambhu, O you whose crown is adorned with the half-moon, O Maheśāna, O wielder of the trident, O wearer of the mass of matted locks!
You alone are the all-pervading one, whose form is the universe.
Be gracious, be gracious, O Lord, whose form is perfect! || 4 ||
The Supreme Self is one, the primordial seed of the universe, effortless, formless, and knowable through the syllable Om;
from whom the universe is born and by whom it is sustained.
I worship that Lord, in whom the entire universe dissolves. || 5 ||
I praise Him who is not earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air, nor space; who is neither lethargy nor sleep;
who is neither heat nor cold; who has no location, no dress, and no physical form—Him who is the threefold form.
The unborn, eternal cause of causes, the auspicious and absolute illuminator of illuminators,
the fourth state beyond darkness, devoid of beginning and end.
I take refuge in the supreme purifier, who is free from duality.
Salutations to you, salutations to you, O All-pervading One, whose form is the universe!
Salutations to you, salutations to you, whose form is consciousness and bliss!
Salutations to you, salutations to you, who are attainable through austerity and yoga!
Salutations to you, salutations to you, O one who is accessible through the knowledge of the Vedas! || 8 ||
O Lord, wielder of the trident, all-pervading one, Lord of the Universe,
Mahādeva, Śambhu, Great Lord, three-eyed one!
O Beloved of Śivā, peaceful one, enemy of Smara, destroyer of the cities!
There is none other than you who is more excellent, worthy of honor, or to be esteemed. || 9 ||
O Śambhu, O Maheśa, O Compassionate One, O Trident-bearer, O Lord of Gaurī, O Lord of Beings, O Destroyer of the bonds of beings!
O Lord of Kāśī, by Your compassion You alone strike, protect, and create this world; You are the Great Lord. (10)
O God Bhava, enemy of Smara, from you the universe arises;
O Mṛḍa, Lord of the Universe, the universe abides in you alone;
O Īśa, this very universe goes to dissolution in you alone.
O Hara, whose nature is the *liṅga*, you who possess the form of the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings! || 11 ||

Thus ends the Vedasāraśivastotra, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, the disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (paramahaṃsaparivrājakācārya).
